# THE GARRISON [italic]The flag on the gate changes. The job does not.[/italic]
## WHO WE ARE GOVFOR, government forces, is whatever unit the governing power has posted to hold this colony. In one rotation it is the Colonial Marines, in the next the Royal Marine Commandos, a Colonial Marshal crisis team, Union troops or Company security working under government contract. Whoever wears the patch answers to the same orders: protect the colony and keep it running.
## CHAIN OF COMMAND - [bold]Commanding officer:[/bold] sets the alert state, the curfew and the security zones, and signs every bulletin on this board. - [bold]Executive officer:[/bold] runs the garrison day to day and answers civilian complaints. - [bold]Staff officers:[/bold] patrol schedules, checkpoint orders, supply and liaison with Colony Administration. - [bold]Squads and patrols:[/bold] the soldiers you will actually meet.
## WHY WE ARE HERE The Neroid Sector is rich, scattered and a long way from help, and no power holds it outright. Since the United Americas pulled back from much of the sector, armed cells flying the Colonial Liberation Front name have grown bolder. The garrison exists to: - defend the colony from dissident and insurgent attack; - respond to fire, collapse, gas and any other mass emergency; - watch the atmosphere and the ground, and sound the alarm early; - secure the colony's power, water, air and landing facilities.
## THE STABLE LESSON In 2168 Drill Site 68-B on Albacetire punctured a ravine of pressurised carbon monoxide. The Carbon Ravine disaster killed more than twelve thousand people, soldiers among them, because nobody was ready for it. The Albacetire Stability Mandate that followed built Joint Base Schaefer, the fort the locals call Stable, and every garrison in the sector learned the same thing: the soldier at the gate is also the first responder.
## STANDING ORDERS TO TROOPS Published so you know what to expect from us. - Identify yourself and your unit when a colonist asks. - Nothing is taken from a civilian without a signed receipt. - Force is the last tool, not the first.
